archetype.name: Game Manager (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 14-year journeyman who wins by getting the ball out on time to short and intermediate targets, staying clean in the pocket and leaning on structure rather than arm talent or legs.

report.headline: A clean, quick-game backup who has slid to third string behind Bagent
report.take:
Case Keenum is what he has been for most of his career: a steady, low-variance passer who keeps an offense on schedule and rarely beats a defense over the top. His 2026 tracking profile looks like his old self. He throws to an intended depth of 7.44 yards, 0.76 yards short of the sticks on average, with a 13.2% aggressiveness rate. Those numbers line up with the 6.9-8.4 aDOT and 16-23% aggressiveness he showed from 2016 to 2019. The CPOE is slightly negative (-0.85), as it has been in every season except his 2017 run in Minnesota. That year is the outlier in his career, not the baseline.

The season is two very different games. Against Philadelphia he started, played every snap and ran an efficient, under-control game plan: 24 of 34, 247 yards, two touchdowns, no sacks and +7.3 passing EPA in a 27-7 win. Against Green Bay he came off the bench behind Tyson Bagent for 33% of the snaps in a 31-7 blowout. He went 11 of 19 for 108 yards with an interception, two sacks and a lost fumble, worth -6.4 EPA. Average those together and you get his middling season ranks (26th in EPA per dropback, 30th in CPOE). Neither game is really the season. The first shows what he can do with a full week and a script. The second shows what happens when he's dropped into a catch-up game.

The splits tell the same story. Within one score he completed 75.9% at +0.35 EPA per play with an 8.6 CPOE. Trailing by nine or more, he fell to -0.568 per play and took both of his sacks. Under center (14 plays) he hit 13 of 14 at +0.818 per play. In shotgun (41 plays) he dropped to -0.394, mostly because the Green Bay snaps came in obvious passing situations. That is a game manager's footprint: good when the run game and play-action are live, limited when he has to push the ball downfield to come back. He was 1 of 4 on throws of 20+ air yards.

The bigger story is his role. The Bears turned to Bagent for Week 5, and as of October 13 the depth chart lists Keenum as QB3. Caleb Williams (93% of snaps when healthy) carries an October 18 return estimate, though Ben Johnson wouldn't commit to Atlanta. Unless injuries pile up, Keenum is an emergency option, not a weekly contributor.

strengths.title: Keeps himself clean and on time
strengths.body: He was pressured on just 5.7% of dropbacks (2nd of 36) and turned none of that pressure into sacks. His bad-throw rate ranks 3rd. That comes from a 2.65-second release, quick reads and a short aim point rather than from great protection. It is a durable trait: his pressure-to-sack rate ranked 8th and 14th in 2018-19 on full seasons.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle is his zone
strengths.body: On throws of 10-19 air yards he produced +0.734 EPA with a 63.6% success rate. Throws to the middle ran +0.318 per play with both touchdowns. This is the classic veteran-backup window: timing throws between the linebackers off play-action. The sample is only 11 intermediate attempts, but it fits how he has always won.

strengths.title: Efficient inside a working script
strengths.body: In one-score games and under center he looks like a functional starter, at +0.35 EPA and +0.818 EPA per play respectively. With a full week as the starter against Philadelphia, he posted +7.3 passing EPA and no sacks.

concerns.title: Third on the depth chart
concerns.body: Bagent started Week 5, and Keenum is now listed as QB3. That is the main reason his outlook is so limited. With Williams trending toward a return, Keenum's path to snaps runs through two injuries or another blowout.

concerns.title: No answer when trailing
concerns.body: Down nine or more, he fell to -0.568 EPA per play, with his interception and both sacks. In shotgun he managed only 56.4% completions. He hit 1 of 4 throws of 20+ air yards. That is not new: his CPOE has been negative in eight of nine logged seasons. He can't flip a game with the deep ball, so a deficit takes away his best tools.

concerns.title: Loose with the ball
concerns.body: His turnover-worthy count includes two fumbles in only 57 dropbacks, and one was lost in the Green Bay relief outing. On a tiny sample this is partly noise, but it shrinks the margin for a player who depends on avoiding mistakes.

trend.note: He went from a clean 24.5-point start against Philadelphia to a -6.4 EPA relief appearance in a Green Bay blowout. The demotion to QB3 followed.

nextGame.headline: Atlanta at QB3: likely a clipboard week
nextGame.body:
If he did play, Atlanta is a poor fit. The Falcons rank 3rd in defensive success rate and 5th against both short and deep throws, which shuts down the short-to-intermediate game he lives on. They hit quarterbacks often (6th in hit rate) but finish few sacks (22nd), which suits his quick release. Offenses throw against them more than anywhere else (1st in pass rate over norm). Even so, QBs score only a mid-pack 18.9 PPR a game against them. They are generous in raw volume but efficient per play.

Availability decides everything here. Williams is listed out with an October 18 return estimate, and Johnson said it could be Atlanta "or after." If Williams can't go, Bagent, who started Week 5, is the next man up ahead of Keenum. RB Kyle Monangai (41% of snaps) is also out, which thins the run game that feeds Chicago's under-center play-action. On Atlanta's side, Michael Penix Jr. (ribs, MRI) is questionable, and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) is questionable. Za'Darius Smith is out and LB Yasir Abdullah is on IR. These are real dents, but none changes the fact that Keenum is unlikely to take meaningful snaps.

keyMatchups.title: Falcons' short-zone discipline vs his checkdowns
keyMatchups.body: His throws of 0-9 air yards already ran negative (-0.117 EPA), and Atlanta allows the 5th-lowest EPA on short throws. Without the intermediate shots, his offense would stall.

keyMatchups.title: Hits without sacks
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta gets home often but rarely finishes. His zero sacks under pressure are the one area where he would match up well. Expect hurried, short completions rather than drive-killing sacks.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams is cleared. If he isn't, Bagent starts, and Keenum stays third unless the game gets out of hand.

restOfSeason.body: As QB3 behind a starter returning from a hamstring strain and the backup who started Week 5, Keenum's expected weekly output is close to zero. His projections reflect that emergency role. If injuries force him into a start, the Philadelphia game and his career suggest roughly 200-250 passing yards with one or two touchdowns when the script is friendly. Expect a sharp drop-off whenever Chicago trails, because he doesn't attack downfield. The clean-pocket and low-sack traits are real and have held for years. The 92.9% under-center completion rate and the intermediate EPA come from small samples and would come down with volume.
swingFactors: Bagent's performance as the next man up
Blowout scripts that empty the bench

confidence.note: Only 57 dropbacks, half in garbage time, and he is QB3 with little chance of snaps.
